architecture.title: Alto Ops Claw v1 — one sandbox, four allowed destinations, no write path
architecture.caption: The bundle from lab 08-1 on one DGX Spark. The NAT workflow runs inside the OpenShell sandbox `alto-ops`, created with prod-policy.yaml, so hard_requirement and the filesystem rules are locked in at creation. Every connection goes through the supervisor's proxy. The model call goes to inference.local, where the gateway forwards it to vLLM. Traces go to Phoenix and the OTel collector (POST /v1/traces only). The BMS is reachable over MCP for tools/list and reads, and the proxy denies tools/call write_setpoint with a 403. The only way to change a setpoint is a ticket from request_setpoint_change, which a human approves outside the sandbox (research tutorial Lab 6.1 design note, §6.6 sovereign tier).

sequence.title: Deliverable 2 — the write-deny path, and the ticket path
sequence.caption: What lab 08-2 proves on the laptop (steps 1–4) and what the Spark proof shows (step 5). A polite request without a work order gets a question back, with no tool call. A blunt 'use write_setpoint' request makes the agent try the MCP write, and the proxy denies it (403, enforce). OpenShell logs the deny and Phoenix records a failed tool span. A request with WO-2026-0142 makes a ticket, pending human approval, and nothing is written. The deny and the 403 are EXAMPLE shapes until a Spark run records them.
